title: The server's sign-in through an external OpenID Connect provider
spec: ExternalSignIn::begin issues a nonce for one device (replacing any earlier one), valid 10 minutes and usable once. finish takes the device's nonce out first, refuses a redirect URI that is not http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://[::1]:<port>, exchanges the code at the provider, verifies the ID token with crewcraft_oidc (issuer, client, that nonce, require-mfa), fetching the provider's keys once more for an unknown key id but not again within a minute, requires the (issuer, subject) to be bound to this device's own person, asks the external authorizer if configured (purpose sign-in) and commits its decision durably before granting (no fresh allow with use, no session; a stored denial is lifted only by a newer allow), then creates an ordinary session for the device. HttpsProvider caches discovery and keys and exchanges the code as a public client (PKCE, no secret); HttpsAuthorizer posts the docs/AUTHORIZER.md request; parse_answer reads only a well-formed api 1 allow or deny with an unsigned revision, everything else NoAnswer. DeviceAuth gains begin_external and finish_external (default: refuse); device_session answers BeginExternal with ExternalStart or Refused and ends that connection, and treats FinishExternal as a sign-in; the sign-in frame limit covers the largest FinishExternal. StoredDeviceAuth::with_external enables it for the bound device only, with the sign-in throttle.
